articles.title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes
articles.summary: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market. Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt.
body: If this makes it sound to you as if there are only a handful of celebrity-friendly homes on earth, and celebrities spend their lives swapping them around among themselves, then you’re right.

According to Mohamed Mussa, the managing director of Chestertons Global, this is partly by design. In an op-ed that has been doing the rounds, Mussa explains that celebrities often require things in properties that civilians like us might not consider, such as gated entrances, secluded grounds, space for staff and layouts designed to keep fans at bay.

“In 2020, Los Angeles City Council passed an ordinance allowing tour buses to be banned from residential streets judged unsafe,” he explains, which has to be useful. I once had a fairly major freakout after buying my house because I didn’t check the details properly and missed that the plumbing under my kitchen sink consisted of an Evian bottle sellotaped to a pipe. Imagine how much worse it would be to buy a house and realise that a packed bus parks outside your front door three times a day so that tourists can try and take a picture of you putting the washing out.
points: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market.

articles.title: Help! Why does my apple pie always have a soggy base? | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: Direct the heat and minimise the moisture to save your pastry from a saturated bottom, says our panel of pie pros. Why does the pastry base of my apple pie always come out soggy? What am I doing wrong?
body: That said, Sophie could always consider including some sort of barrier, too, says Dee Rettali, co-founder of Fortitude Bakehouse in London: “My mother was an amazing baker, and she always sprinkled a very fine crumble mix [just sugar and flour, no fat] on the bottom of her pie before putting in any fruit. That will then absorb most of the liquid.”

On to the bake itself, and Rettali always pops her tin on a baking stone in the oven, because “it really conducts heat into the bottom of the pie”. Franklin, however, thinks that’s a “slightly unnecessary step”. The reason? “It puts a barrier between the base of the pie and the direct heat.” Instead, he simply slides the tin straight on to a rack in the oven: “It will just cook better.”

Gummy, undercooked pastry can also be avoided simply by baking the pie for a bit longer, Franklin says: “With the exception of my own cookbooks, of course, I never think pie recipes give the right cooking times. Always give yourself an extra 10 minutes.” After all, not every home oven is as hot as it says on the dial. And a large pie, Franklin adds, is going to take at least 40 minutes.

articles.title: John H. Powers III to Lead NIAID Amid Turmoil
articles.summary: Dr. John H. Powers III was appointed director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a powerful post held for decades by Dr. Anthony Fauci.
body: Dr. John H. Powers III was appointed on Monday to lead the National Institutes of Health division on infectious diseases, giving him control of a politically contentious agency with a budget of over $6.5 billion and responsibility for research into such pressing threats as measles and Ebola.

His designation as director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a position held for nearly four decades by Dr. Anthony S. Fauci, caps a rapid rise for Dr. Powers, who until recently was an N.I.H. contractor and clinical trials design specialist.

Since the start of the second Trump administration, Dr. Powers gained influence among senior health officials as he was tapped to study vaccine injuries, a priority of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Early last year, Dr. Powers worked with Dr. Matthew Memoli, the No. 2 official at the N.I.H. and a critic of Covid vaccine mandates, to obtain sets of data related to vaccines and autism from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, according to emails reviewed by The New York Times.

articles.title: Measles Is Officially Back in the United States. What Now?
articles.summary: A patient with a measles rash in Texas last year. The number of cases in the United States this year has topped 5,400, more than double last year’s tally and the highest since 1991, nearly a decade before the country attained elimination status.
body: The United States has returned to a time, until recently unimaginable, when measles is a persistent threat, not just a sporadic one that can easily be snuffed out.

Even with rigorous effort, it is likely to take years to regain measles elimination status, which the country officially lost on Tuesday. In the meantime, Americans will need to embrace strategies, some well worn and some new, to contend with this forgotten menace, more than a dozen experts said in interviews.

Local and state health departments will need more resources to combat outbreaks. Doctors, parents and teachers will need to familiarize themselves with the symptoms, and prepare to quarantine anyone who is unvaccinated and exposed for 21 days. Hospitals will need to prepare for an onslaught of patients infected with a highly contagious virus. Public health officials may need new tools to detect, diagnose and stem outbreaks quickly. And they may need to revise the recommended vaccination schedule to protect the most vulnerable.
“We’re really in kind of a new Wild West of our own making,” said Dr. Christopher Monson, an intensive care pediatrician at the University of Rochester.

articles.title: It’s chicken salad season! Three bright and flavourful recipes by Danielle Alvarez
articles.summary: The Sydney chef shares a trio of recipes, including a Vietnamese-ish combo and a kale salad that you’ll actually enjoy. Bright, sour, salty, a little sweet and also on the lighter side, this is the kind of thing I crave pretty regularly.
body: Feel free to make this with pork instead of chicken, and cook the meatballs on an outdoor grill when it’s too hot to turn the stove on.

To make the meatballs, combine the garlic, chilli, lemongrass, coriander and mint in a food processor and blitz until very finely minced. Scoop the paste into a large bowl. Add the remaining meatball ingredients to the bowl and mix everything together. The mixture will feel very wet – for easier handling, you can place it in the fridge to firm up; it also helps to moisten your hands with a little oil before shaping.

Form the mixture into balls, using about two tablespoons of the mixture for each meatball. Set them on a tray and place back in the fridge if you’re not cooking them right away. You can make the meatballs a day in advance, or freeze for convenience; just add a few extra minutes of cooking time if cooking from frozen.
To make the dressing, crush the garlic and chilli together using a mortar and pestle. Scrape into a bowl, add the remaining dressing ingredients and stir to dissolve the sugar.

articles.title: Fearing Chinese Rivals, U.S. Biotech Adopts a New Norm: Share Nothing
articles.summary: Fears that Chinese companies will seize on biotech discoveries in the U.S. and quickly beat them to market with their own inventions or slightly altered dupes have prompted American companies to keep their discoveries secret.
body: It used to be that companies and scientists with ideas for new drugs couldn’t wait to announce their discoveries at meetings, in preprints and on their websites.

Researchers at the biotechnology firm Alnylam Pharmaceuticals have an unwritten policy: Do not reveal early-stage studies or discuss unpublished data, according to its founding chief executive, Dr. Christoph Westphal.

Jacob Becraft of Strand Therapeutics delays filing for patents to keep his company’s discoveries secret. And he is careful about disclosing his company’s intellectual property and confidential material, even to investors.
Alexis Borisy, a co-founder of Curie.Bio, which helps early-stage biotechs, says he tells scientists to “go dark” — don’t publish, don’t present posters at meetings, don’t even go to meetings.

articles.title: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
articles.summary: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.
body: Measles has come roaring back in the United States, as vaccination rates have fallen and cases of the once-extinguished virus have soared. That backslide has now cost the nation its measles elimination status, after the virus spread uninterrupted for more than a year.

“It’s a giant stain on our reputation,” said Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the Pandemic Center at the Brown University School of Public Health. “Everyone ought to be just utterly disgusted by the willing return back to an age of death and high cost.”

The announcement, made Tuesday by the Pan American Health Organization, ushers in a new era in which major outbreaks could routinely disrupt communities around the nation, sickening thousands of children. It also marks a highly embarrassing reversal for a country that showed the rest of the world it was possible to rein in the wildly contagious virus when it won elimination status in 2000.

articles.title: Inside the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Premiere, Where the Odds Were in Everyone’s Favor
articles.summary: On Monday evening, Lincoln Center was temporarily transformed into the Capitol of Panem for the highly anticipated world premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
body: The dress theme for the evening, Make Them Remember You, encouraged attendees to dress in vintage-leaning silhouettes and rich textures, and to embrace a touch of theatricality. It was an assignment that the cast and attendees alike took seriously, donning looks that were hard to forget. Elle Fanning and Elizabeth Banks took on a battle of the Effies, with each actress indulging in an avant-garde approach to the mood board. McKenna Grace’s Mockingjay gown came complete with wings as a nod to Katniss’s costume from Catching Fire. The horde of onlookers surrounding the area also displayed their own interpretations of Capitol-inspired garb.

As the final guests were ushered into Alice Tully Hall, director Francis Lawrence invited what he described as “one of the most impressive casts in cinema” to rise one by one. Each familiar face from the original films—including Woody Harrelson, Josh Hutcherson, and Jennifer Lawrence—was greeted with thunderous applause. Francis even invited the audience to wish his assistant a quick “Happy Birthday” before the lights dimmed and the room erupted into more cheers as each member of the cast appeared on screen.

articles.title: Kate Middleton And Prince William Turn to Bollywood Fashion Royalty in Mumbai
articles.summary: At the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards, Kate Middleton wore a hand-embroidered anarkali by Mahima Mahajan, while Prince William opted for a bandhgala by couturier and Bollywood costume design legend Manish Malhotra.
body: The Prince and Princess of Wales ’s second official visit to India reached its high point today, as William hosted the sixth annual Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai. The event, which awards £1 million ($1.3 million) each to five winners tackling the world’s most pressing environmental challenges, was held on the subcontinent in recognition of the fact that it has offered more winners and finalists than anywhere else since the initiative was founded in 2020. It also marked Catherine’s first appearance at the awards since Boston in 2022, with the couple marking the occasion with a rare red-carpet (or, in this case, green) photo call.

And while the Princess’s wardrobe over the past few days has largely consisted of her tried-and-tested staples—a Roksanda dress here, an Edeline Lee suit there—tonight was the night to pull out all the stops. Catherine chose a hand-embroidered anarkali of sindoori-red georgette by New Delhi-based designer Mahima Mahajan, which she paired with a necklace and earrings from Queen Elizabeth II’s emerald tassel suite and a burgundy velvet Prada minaudière.

articles.title: This Buzzy New Wellness Retreat in Kerala Blends Ancient Traditions With Modern Medicine
articles.summary: Blending full-body medical scans with Ayurvedic pulse readings, the groundbreaking new retreat Tulåh in Kerala offers a 360-degree approach to longevity.
body: As the birthplace of yoga and its sister science Ayurveda, India certainly has no shortage of wellness retreats. The country is quite literally filled with spiritual centers, located everywhere from the foothills of the Himalayas to the beaches of Goa to the sacred riverbanks of Varanasi. I’ve been fortunate enough to visit a fair amount of them over the past decade, thanks to both my work as the author of Destination Wellness, an exploration of ancient health traditions around the world, and the fact that my husband is a born-and-raised Delhiite. We live in New York, but go to India regularly to stay with family and travel around the rest of the country together.

articles.title: Applications for the 2027 LVMH Prize Are Now Open
articles.summary: Since 2013, the LVMH Prize has served as an invaluable opportunity for young designers. Applications for the 14th edition are open now through April 4, 2027.
body: Each year in Paris, promising young designers present their work to industry legends, hoping to distinguish themselves as part of fashion’s rising new guard—and to secure a cash prize of €400,000. Today, applications for the 14th edition of the LVMH Prize are now open.

Over the length of the Prize, the event has served as an invaluable launchpad for independent designers, including two former contestants who are both set to make historic debuts. Grace Wales Bonner (winner, 2016) will present her first collection for Hermès men’s in January, 2027, and just last week, Martine Rose (semifinalist, 2017) was confirmed for the top job at Balenciaga following Pierpaolo Piccioli’s departure. Meanwhile, this year’s Karl Lagerfeld prize winner, Zane Li of Lii, also snagged the top prize at the 2026 CFDA/ Vogue Fashion Fund.
